To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inclusion of a kinematical restriction in the GC3 method allows us to detect fainter streams in the presence of realistic observational errors and a realistic Galactic background.

the proposed extension of the GC 3 method allows the identification of satellite streams in the presence of a realistic galactic background, observational errors and phase mixing, provided we use data with high astrometric precision.

the inclusion of velocity information, as seen from the Galactic centre, in the search for stellar streams in the sky, vastly enhances their contrast against the background, even with observational errors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of stellar remnants of accreted satellites in the Galactic halo.
the detection of satellite remnants in the Galactic halo using the future Gaia astrometric database.
the detection of the remnants of accreted satellites in the Galactic halo with the future Gaia mission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the inclusion of kinematical information in the search of satellite remnants in the Gaia database is very promising and will be very useful in the search for the debris of the dwarf galaxies that have been accreted by the Milky Way.

the method is capable of recovering the remnants of satellites with initial mass 10 8 - 10 9 L, with star formation histories different from those of the background, and with orbits that are not too eccentric.
our method can recover satellites with initial masses in the range of a few times 10 6 ; 10 7 ; M, and ages in the range 2 ; 10 8 ; 10 9 years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the feasibility to detect and characterize the remnants of accreted satellite galaxies using the Gaia database.

our method is able to recover satellites with a mass as low as 10 8 ; M⊙, with star formation histories that are significantly different from those of the Galactic background, provided they are still bound to the Milky Way.
the GC3+ method, as presented here, will be able to detect and identify most of the Galactic satellites with luminosities above 10 7 ; L⊙, even in the case of a very low mass merger.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GC3 method can be used with Gaia data to detect the debris from the disrupted dwarf galaxies, even in the crowded Galactic environment, provided that the streamer is sufficiently luminous.
the kinematical extension of the GC method will be a powerful tool for identifying and characterizing the Galactic halo in the Gaia era.

, even with a modest amount of observational errors, a method based only on the sky positions of the stars will be insufficient to detect the remnants of the Galactic dwarf spheroidal satellites in the future Gaia data base.
